nodes.name: Fire — county sales-tax pass-through
nodes.note: The amount is sourced, but this is only the county's slice of fire funding. Rural Arkansas fire departments are typically funded primarily through fire protection districts' own millage and dues, plus city budgets — the county pass-through is a slice, not the whole picture. The full fire map (district budgets + dues + city FD + this line) does not yet exist in public, navigable form. That is Docket #4, and it is a prerequisite for framing any fire-funding question honestly.

nodes.name: Property tax — millage rates
nodes.note: Now sourced from the state's 2025 millage book (for 2026 collections). County: 7.1 mills — road 3.0, library 1.0, hospital 1.0, college 1.0, plus small general/misc mills that split differently for city and rural residents (exact column mapping still being confirmed against the book's layout). City of Arkadelphia adds 5.0; Gurdon 5.4. Schools are the big share: Arkadelphia district 47.65, Gurdon 43.0. Total inside Arkadelphia city limits: 59.75 mills. A $100,000 home is assessed at 20% ($20,000), so one mill costs about $20 a year — 59.75 mills is roughly $1,195 before the homestead credit. Notable: the Arkadelphia school rate rose from 44.65 in the 2024 book to 47.65 in the 2025 book — 3.0 new bond mills.

nodes.name: Sales taxes
nodes.note: At least two dedicated sales taxes are visible from the spending side (EDCCC economic development; Various Fire Departments fund). Rates, sunset dates, and enacting ordinances not yet ingested. This got more urgent in July 2026: local reporting says the county owes the state roughly $1.3 million in sales-tax rebate repayments — a news lead, not yet a document in this corpus. The enacting ordinances live in the county's online ordinance archive (Docket #9).

nodes.name: State turnback, fees, fines, grants
nodes.note: Highway turnback, court fees and fines, automation fees, and grant revenue are implied by the fund names but not itemized in the ordinance. Treasurer's reports and the legislative audit carry this detail.

nodes.name: City of Arkadelphia
nodes.note: The city's budget document is still not posted online — but its audited financials are, and they are now in the document library (FY2022–FY2024, plus the water & sewer system audit). FY2024, regulatory basis: general fund revenues $18.2M, expenditures $13.2M, year-end fund balance $2.3M. Budget line items and salaries remain a city hall records request.

nodes.name: Arkadelphia Public Schools (+ Gurdon)
nodes.note: School millage IS the largest line on most residents' tax bills, and it is now sourced: Arkadelphia district 47.65 mills (25.0 M&O + 2.0 other M&O + 17.65 bond + 3.0 other bond), Gurdon 43.0. Both districts' FY2024 audits are in the document library; the Arkadelphia district has pledged property taxes against $35.05M in bonds issued 2021–2022. District budget detail is the remaining gap.

nodes.name: Fire protection districts
nodes.note: The funding structure is now mapped: Clark County levies no fire millage (the state millage book shows none in the county breakdown), so rural departments run on dues, donations, and the county's $45,921 sales-tax pass-through, while the Arkadelphia FD is funded inside the city's budget. Departments identified so far: Arkadelphia FD, East Clark County Rural VFD, Okolona VFD, Whelen Springs VFD, and the Clark County Fire Association, a small 501(c)(3) that files only postcard returns. What remains offline: each department's dues schedule and finances — still the counter-visit half of Docket #4.
